title: TransFORM-TMD: a feasibility device trial
official: TransFORM-TMD: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation FOR Myalgia TemporoMandibular Disorder and depression: a parallel-arm, double-blind, randomised, sham-controlled, feasibility device trial
summary:
Background and study aims
Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) are musculoskeletal conditions affecting the jaw joint and jaw muscles. Some people experience persistent painful myalgia TMD, where symptoms last for more than three months and can have a significant impact on daily life. Depression is also common in people with TMD. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is a non-invasive treatment that delivers electrical stimulation to the vagus nerve through the ear and has shown potential benefits in other painful conditions and in depression. This study aims to assess whether it is feasible to conduct a larger clinical trial of self-delivered taVNS in people with persistent myalgia TMD and depression, and to explore its effects on symptoms, autonomic function and inflammatory markers.

Who can participate?
Adults aged 18 years and over with persistent myalgia temporomandibular disorder lasting at least three months, who have completed TMD self-management for at least six weeks and are able to provide written informed consent in English.

What does the study involve?
Participants are randomised to receive either a taVNS device or a sham device. Participants use the device at home for 12 weeks. The study is double-blinded, meaning participants do not know which device they have been allocated. Assessments are conducted over the 12-week study period.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
The protocol states that the study will collect evidence on whether taVNS is likely to be helpful for people with TMD and depression. 

Risks not provided at time of registration

Where is the study run from?
Newcastle Dental Clinical Research Facility, Newcastle upon Tyne, England.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
November 2026 to November 2027.

Who is funding the study?
NIHR Newcastle Biomedical Research Centre and NIHR North East and North Cumbria Regional Research Delivery Network, UK.

Who is the main contact?
Dr James Allison, Newcastle University, james.allison@newcastle.ac.uk.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	≥ 18 years of age
2.	Able to provide written informed consent in English
3.	Diagnosis of persistent (≥3-month duration) myalgia temporomandibular disorder, according to international brief Diagnostic Criteria for Temporomandibular Disorders (bDC/TMD)
4.	Completed TMD self-management for ≥ 6 weeks
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Current participation in another interventional trial
2.	Non-myalgia TMD as the primary TMD complaint
3.	Current orofacial pain other than TMD or oral disease likely to cause pain (e.g., untreated dental disease, neuropathic pain, trigeminal neuralgia)
4.	Previous vagotomy
5.	Long-term use of corticosteroids or immunomodulatory biological therapies (e.g., to treat inflammatory disorders)
6.	Bipolar affective disorder, psychotic disorder or personality disorder
7.	Dementia
8.	Primary neurological injury (e.g., axonal injury, stroke or traumatic brain injury) or disorder (e.g., Parkinson’s disease)
9.	Myocardial infarction (MI) within the previous 6 months
10.	History of cardiac disease (e.g., cardiomyopathy, arrhythmia, prolonged QT interval)
11.	Active implanted device at the ear, heart (e.g., pacemaker), or stimulating the nervous system (e.g., implanted VNS, other neurostimulator)
12.	Pregnancy
13.	Not fluent in English
sponsor: Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
